verses.text: And Adam had relations with his wife Eve, and she conceived and gave birth to Cain. "With the help of the LORD I have brought forth a man," she said.
Later she gave birth to Cain's brother Abel. Now Abel was a keeper of sheep, while Cain was a tiller of the soil.
So in the course of time, Cain brought some of the fruit of the soil as an offering to the LORD,
while Abel brought the best portions of the firstborn of his flock. And the LORD looked with favor on Abel and his offering,
but He had no regard for Cain and his offering. So Cain became very angry, and his countenance fell.
"Why are you angry," said the LORD to Cain, "and why has your countenance fallen?
If you do what is right, will you not be accepted? But if you refuse to do what is right, sin is crouching at your door; it desires you, but you must master it."
Then Cain said to his brother Abel, "Let us go out to the field." And while they were in the field, Cain rose up against his brother Abel and killed him.
And the LORD said to Cain, "Where is your brother Abel?" "I do not know!" he answered. "Am I my brother's keeper?"
"What have you done?" replied the LORD. "The voice of your brother's blood cries out to Me from the ground.
Now you are cursed and banished from the ground, which has opened its mouth to receive your brother's blood from your hand.
When you till the ground, it will no longer yield its produce to you. You will be a fugitive and a wanderer on the earth."
But Cain said to the LORD, "My punishment is greater than I can bear.
Behold, this day You have driven me from the face of the earth, and from Your face I will be hidden; I will be a fugitive and a wanderer on the earth, and whoever finds me will kill me."
"Not so!" replied the LORD. "If anyone slays Cain, then Cain will be avenged sevenfold." And the LORD placed a mark on Cain, so that no one who found him would kill him.
So Cain went out from the presence of the LORD and settled in the land of Nod, east of Eden.
And Cain had relations with his wife, and she conceived and gave birth to Enoch. Then Cain built a city and named it after his son Enoch.
Now to Enoch was born Irad, and Irad was the father of Mehujael, and Mehujael was the father of Methusael, and Methusael was the father of Lamech.
And Lamech married two women, one named Adah and the other Zillah.
Adah gave birth to Jabal; he was the father of those who dwell in tents and raise livestock.
And his brother's name was Jubal; he was the father of all who play the harp and flute.
And Zillah gave birth to Tubal-cain, a forger of every implement of bronze and iron. And the sister of Tubal-cain was Naamah.
Then Lamech said to his wives: "Adah and Zillah, hear my voice; wives of Lamech, listen to my speech. For I have slain a man for wounding me, a young man for striking me.
If Cain is avenged sevenfold, then Lamech seventy-sevenfold."
And Adam again had relations with his wife, and she gave birth to a son and named him Seth, saying, "God has granted me another seed in place of Abel, since Cain killed him."
And to Seth also a son was born, and he called him Enosh. At that time men began to call upon the name of the LORD.

context.author: Genesis names no author. Jewish and Christian tradition, and the New Testament’s way of speaking of “the Law of Moses” (Luke 24:44), credit the five books of the Law to Moses. Many scholars think Genesis was gathered and shaped from older sources over a long time, and a few remarks look back from a later day: “at that time the Canaanites were in the land” (Genesis 12:6).
context.genre: Narrative of beginnings (Genesis 1-11): creation, the first family, the flood and the nations, with genealogies
context.audience: Israel, God’s covenant people, learning who their God is, where the world came from and what went wrong with it
context.setting: Eve bears Cain and then Abel; Cain works the ground and Abel keeps flocks (vv.1-2). Both bring offerings. “The LORD looked with favor on Abel and his offering, but He had no regard for Cain and his offering,” and Cain is very angry (vv.4-5). God warns him: “sin is crouching at your door. It desires you, but you must master it” (v.7). Cain kills Abel in the field (v.8). “Where is your brother Abel?” “I do not know,” Cain replies. “Am I my brother’s keeper?” (v.9). Abel’s blood cries out from the ground (v.10), and Cain is driven out to be a wanderer, but God puts a mark on him so no one will kill him (vv.11-15). He settles in the land of Nod, east of Eden, and builds a city (vv.16-17). His descendants make tents, music and bronze and iron tools, and Lamech boasts of killing a man (vv.19-24). Then Seth is born, and “at that time men began to call upon the name of the LORD” (v.26).
context.custom: The farmer and the shepherd were the two ways of life of the ancient Near East, often at odds. The firstborn of a flock and its fat portions (v.4) were the best part, later required for God (Exodus 13:12; Leviticus 3:16). Under the law of the clan, a killing called for a kinsman to avenge the blood; God’s mark protects even a murderer from endless revenge (v.15), but Lamech boasts that he will be avenged seventy-seven times (v.24).
context.timelineImmediate: Chapter 5 lists ten generations from Adam to Noah, the line of Seth.
context.timelineBible: Genesis does not say why Abel’s offering was accepted. Hebrews says it was by faith (Hebrews 11:4), and John says Cain’s deeds were evil and his brother’s righteous (1 John 3:12). Jesus speaks of the blood of righteous Abel (Matthew 23:35), and Hebrews says the blood of Jesus “speaks a better word than the blood of Abel” (Hebrews 12:24). Jesus answers Lamech’s seventy-seven-fold revenge with forgiveness “seventy-seven times” (Matthew 18:22).

translation.meaning: His name sounds like the Hebrew for breath or vapor (the key word of Ecclesiastes). His life was short.
Sin; also a sin offering. Its first use in the Bible pictures sin as an animal crouching at the door.
To keep, guard, watch over. The man was put in the garden to keep it (2:15); Cain refuses to keep his brother.

gospelParallels.note: By faith Abel offered God a better sacrifice than Cain.
Not like Cain, who belonged to the evil one.
The sprinkled blood that speaks a better word than Abel’s.

otBackground.note: The LORD hates hands that shed innocent blood.
He who avenges blood remembers them.

mapCoords.placeName: The land of Nod, east of Eden (location unknown)

overview.summary: Cain kills his brother Abel out of anger and envy; God judges him but protects him, Cain’s line builds a city and makes tools and music, and with Seth people begin to call on the LORD.
overview.placeName: The land of Nod, east of Eden (location unknown)

history.t: Two ways of life side by side.

customs.t: The best of the flock belonged to God.

archaeology.t: Walled towns like Jericho appear thousands of years before writing.
Lyres were found in the royal tombs of Ur, about 2500 BC.

overview.discussion: Cain asked, “Am I my brother’s keeper?” (v.9). Whose wellbeing has God put in my keeping, and how have I answered?
overview.book: The book of Genesis · 50 chapters (1-25 in the app so far). Beginnings: creation, the fall, the flood and the nations, then God’s promise to Abraham and his family.
overview.author: Moses, by tradition

biblePlaces.name: Eden (location unknown; Genesis names the Tigris and Euphrates)
